question.text: A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is moving with an initial speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The body stops after <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> due to friction between body and the floor. The value of the coefficient of friction is: (Take acceleration due to gravity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
Friction force wil act opposite to the motion of the body.

F=μN=μmg

⇒a=-μg-ve sign for direction relative to the motion of body

Now, applying equation of motion, we get

v=u+at

⇒0=20+-μ×10×5

⇒50μ=20

 ⇒μ=0.4
